name: Oluwanifemi Felix Oyeniyi
feedback: D1 is one of the stronger catalogues I have graded. You captured nine of the ten findings with a quoted evidence line and a correct OWASP plus CWE pairing for each: SQLi (F1, A03 CWE-89, login.php line ~55, capture 02:15:31), MD5 no salt (F8, A02 CWE-916), JWT alg:none (F3, A07 CWE-347, Token 2), hard-coded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (F7, CWE-798), no token expiry (F4, CWE-613), stored XSS (F5, CWE-79, beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443 at 02:18:47), XXE (F2, CWE-611), open redirect (F6, CWE-601) and path traversal (your F10, CWE-22, capture 02:24:02 root:x:0:0). The single missing finding is the cookie flag issue, the session cookie set with no Secure or SameSite (A05, CWE-614), so add that as a tenth card. Where you lost the most ground is the decoy. The construct the brief wanted you to disprove was the SAFE one, the HS256 verify branch that uses hash_equals for a constant-time signature compare and the b64url helpers that only encode. You needed to name that construct and prove at the mechanism level that it is sound, that hash_equals is constant-time so that branch is fine and the real bugs are alg:none and the hard-coded secret. Instead you spent the decoy section resolving whether path traversal is the same root cause as XXE, which is good security reasoning and the right verdict, but it is not the decoy. You did avoid the trap of calling alg:none the decoy, which is correct, since Token 2 is a live unsigned token honoured by the shared service. D2 is excellent. The chain runs in order across all eight hops, each reconciled to a capture line (02:14:08 recon, 02:14:55 failed guess, 02:15:31 SQLi, 02:16:04 the 312-row pull, 02:18:47 XSS, 02:21:13 redirect, 02:23:41 and 02:24:02 the parallel XXE and file read, then the forgery), with a verbatim curl or tool PoC at every hop and the senior insight that the forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service. Your CVSS vectors are complete and justified throughout, which is exactly what earns full marks. One vector to revisit: F1 SQLi should be AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N for about 9.1, not A:H for 9.8, because the authentication bypass does not degrade availability. Impact is well done: 312 customers, balances from the sample up to 950k NGN extrapolated to tens of millions, with the extrapolation assumption stated and tied to the BoltCash launch six weeks out. D3 is strong. The executive summary is jargon-free and lands on the customers-and-naira headline, the threat model names the asset, attacker profile, attack surface and the trust-boundary failure, and your remediation is correctly ordered by effort and chain-breaking rather than by raw CVSS, the F1 plus F8 same-file grouping and F7 plus F3 same-PR grouping are the right instinct. Two gaps: your disproved-decoy section again addresses path traversal rather than the safe hash_equals construct, so it does not state the brief's actual decoy, and your two detection stopgaps name the exact field to watch (the SQL metacharacter patterns in the login POST body, and the alg and exp fields in the Authorization header) but neither gives a false-positive rate, which the rubric asks for. Add an expected FP rate to each rule. D4 owns the decision cleanly, disclose immediately, in your own voice, anchored to the 05-exfil-sample.csv 312 records, with Canon I and Canon II of the ISC2 code cited by number and load-bearing and the NDPA 2023 72-hour notification duty tied to the 312 customers. The shortfall is coverage of the four prompts: you answered the put-it-in-writing prompt and the one-action-regardless-of-manager prompt well, but you did not address the journalist prompt or the colleague-evidence prompt, so write a short paragraph on each. I looked hard for a reason to push this into the 90s and the evidence did not support it, the missed decoy in both D1 and D3, the missing cookie finding, the absent FP rates and the two unanswered ethics prompts are real losses. The single most important fix is to identify and disprove the actual decoy, the safe constant-time hash_equals HS256 verify branch, and prove it sound at the mechanism level rather than analysing path traversal.
